title: Argo grids start after the North Pacific sigma0 26.5 outcrop region freshened; its 2018-2025 lightening came with less Oyashio water and geostrophic salt, no resolved heat input (RG Argo, 2004-2025)
abstract: Question: earlier work found that the late-winter sigma0 26.5 outcrop of the western North Pacific (box W, 36-48 N, 145 E-180) became lighter, first by freshening and after 2018 by warming, and that O2 on 26.5 followed. Local Ekman transport, local E-P, climate modes and front shifts did not explain the freshening. Did geostrophic advection supply it? Approach: monthly salt, heat and density budgets of box W (0-100, 0-200, 0-400 dbar; also box OB) for 2004-2025 from the Roemmich-Gilson Argo grid, with TEOS-10 geostrophic velocity, NCEP R1 stress and heat flux, GPCP precipitation and JRA-3Q fluxes. A plan and two amendments were hashed before the terms they test were computed. Results: RG agrees with World Ocean Database late-winter salinity (r = 0.94), but box W was already fresh in 2004-2006 (WOD change to 2007-2017 only -0.027 psu), so the Argo grid cannot date the freshening and the main geostrophic test failed. In the Argo era the lightening was thermal: 0-200 dbar sigma0 fell 0.057 and 0.065 kg/m3 as temperature rose 0.34 and 0.71 deg C; salinity rose 0.067 psu after 2018. Resolved geostrophic flow gives 62-134% of the post-2018 salt rise (T6 passed) but no net heat (-0.13 to +0.25 deg C of 0.55-0.79 deg C in six box and layer choices), because mean-flow and anomalous-flow heat terms cancel; the geostrophic density term made the water denser (A1 failed). Box W lost 7.8 W/m2 more heat to the air in 2018-2025 in JRA-3Q and 8.2 W/m2 in corrected NCEP R1 (raw R1 +2.9; the JRA-3Q minus R1 offset shifted by -14 W/m2 after 2020, as the documented R1 error predicts). The pre-registered accumulated air-sea test passed with R1 but failed with JRA-3Q, so it is inconclusive. Exploratory: the change was largest at 36-45 N, 142-160 E; salinity on 26.5 rose 0.11 psu in the Oyashio box; the area of Oyashio-type water in box W fell from 37% to 31% and follows box density (r = 0.85). Interpretation: the freshening is older than Argo and its cause stays open; the second outcrop lightening was an ocean-driven warm, salty replacement of Oyashio water with heat from unresolved (eddy and frontal) transport. Limitations: smoothed 1-degree grid, large residual, no formal intervals, 22-yr record, accumulated metric sensitive to flux offsets.

display.caption: Box W (36-48 N, 145 E-180). a, b: late-winter 0-30 m salinity and sigma0 from WOD ship and Argo casts (sci:bfaf6c90, anomaly vs 1975-1989, 95% interval) and from the RG Argo grid (offset to the WOD 2004-2025 mean). The surface was already fresh in 2004-2006. c: RG 0-200 dbar annual sigma0 anomaly and its temperature and salinity parts; the Argo-era lightening is thermal and salinity rose after 2018.

Box W 0-200 dbar density budget from RG, NCEP R1 and GPCP. a: accumulated monthly anomalies (13-month means). b: pre-registered contributions to the 2018-2025 minus 2007-2017 change. Geostrophic advection adds salt (denser) and almost no net heat; the residual (unresolved eddy and frontal transport, mixing, errors) carries the lightening. The accumulated air-sea term depends on the flux product (JRA-3Q gives the opposite sign; see text), so its sign here is not robust.

RG change from 2007-2017 to 2018-2025: late-winter 0-30 m temperature (with mean surface geostrophic flow), salinity and sigma0, and salinity on sigma0 26.5. The warm, salty change is largest at 36-45 N, 142-160 E, where Oyashio-type water retreated.
